# Portosinusoidal vascular disorder

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Gastroenterology > Diseases of the liver > Portosinusoidal vascular disorder*

[Original Article Link](/library/QC0u7R)

---

## Summary

Portosinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD) is a rare noncirrhotic <u>portal hypertension</u> syndrome characterized by lesions involving the portal <u>venules</u> and/or sinusoids. PSVD unifies several older diagnoses and histological patterns (e.g., <u>idiopathic</u> noncirrhotic <u>portal hypertension</u>, hepatoportal <u>sclerosis</u>, incomplete septal <u>cirrhosis</u>) under one umbrella diagnosis. Patients typically have <u>portal hypertension</u> with preserved <u>hepatic function</u> and <u>biopsies</u> that show vascular or architectural remodeling without <u>cirrhosis</u>. Causes include immunological disorders, infections, drugs (e.g., <u>oxaliplatin</u>, <u>azathioprine</u>), and genetic factors. Diagnosis requires a <u>liver biopsy</u> to exclude <u>cirrhosis</u> and identify histological lesions. Patients are often asymptomatic but may present with <u>clinical features of portal hypertension</u> (e.g., <u>variceal bleeding</u>, <u>splenomegaly</u>). Management focuses on treating underlying conditions and managing <u>portal hypertension</u>.
